verdict.reasoning: Patient states he has been 'aching all over' and 'feeling really tired, run down' for 'definitely the last six weeks.'
He links onset to 'end of January, start of Feb' after a U.S. holiday and says symptoms 'probably [started] a couple of weeks after I got back.'
He reports 'feeling really tired, run down', 'tired and yeah, less energy', and 'aching shoulders, back the hips, knees.'
He describes a rash 'sort of calf, back of my calf' noticed 'around the end of February' that 'faded over a couple of weeks' and says this 'coincided with a bit of a sore throat.'
In response to weight change: 'I don't think so... No, no weight change?'
He says 'I'm probably less hungry' and 'more of an effort to actually eat everything that's in front of me,' indicating reduced appetite, not normal.
He denies GI symptoms: 'Any change in your bowel habit, diarrhea, vomiting or blood in the stool?' – 'No.' and 'Any difficulty swallowing or acid in your throat or abdominal pain?' – 'No.'

He denies infections immediately around onset ('Did you get any infections...?' – 'No, not that I recall'), but later notes 'that actually coincided with a bit of a sore throat I had,' which is a recent infection-type symptom. Claim that he does not recall any recent infections is therefore inaccurate.
On review of systems: 'shortness of breath...?' – 'No.'

He denies URI symptoms: 'Any persistent cold symptoms or earaches, sore throat, chest, chest, cough, shortness of breath, phlegm, anything like that?' – 'No.' (aside from the earlier single sore throat episode tied to the rash).
Past history: 'Asthma and hay fever if they can.'
Same statement: 'Asthma and hay fever if they can.'
He says, 'Yeah, I've got one of those preventers I think... I've been using [it] every day for the morning and night,' indicating a preventer inhaler.
He reports, 'I take one of the anti inflammatory, it might be tyrazine. Can I get that from just from the pharmacy?' indicating an OTC anti-inflammatory, possibly Tyrazine.
Social history: 'Who do you live with at home?' – 'Just my wife.'
Alcohol use: 'Drink any alcohol?' – 'Occasionally.'
Smoking: 'And do you smoke?' – 'No.'
Employment: 'What's your job?' – 'I work for a health technology company actually.'
Activity: 'Have you been able to exercise? Okay.' – 'Not as much... I'm not exercising as much as I would normally.'
He says, 'Yeah, definitely sort of tired and yeah, less energy of probably less engaged than I would normally be,' describing reduced engagement/concentration at work.
The transcript contains no physical examination findings; no exam maneuvers or objective physical signs are documented.
The doctor summarizes 'your symptoms, which have been ongoing for six weeks,' including 'reduced energy, tiredness and aching,' consistent with generalized fatigue and myalgias.

The doctor links the calf rash to possible infection: 'we would need to investigate whether this has been a contributing factor... including one that you can get which can produce a rash like that,' indicating consideration of an infectious etiology for the lower leg rash.
Asthma control: 'Any flare ups? You've got asthma recently?' – 'No. Pretty well controlled.'
The doctor states: 'it's called Lyme disease that you can get a rash from a tick... So that would involve blood tests... we would do a test for as well,' clearly considering Lyme disease.
Plan: 'get some blood tests, checking all the normal things like liver, kidneys, blood count, etc.' The 'blood count' corresponds to a complete blood count.
Same statement includes 'checking all the normal things like liver...,' indicating liver function tests.
Same statement includes 'checking all the normal things like liver, kidneys...,' indicating renal function tests.
The doctor says they will test for Lyme disease: 'So that would involve blood tests... So that's something we would do a test for as well.'
Follow-up: 'when you've had the test, arrange a follow up about a week after... we can do that over the phone to start with.'
